 Adhya Sarna Updated: Oct 28, 2026, 14:04 IST Diwali holidays in Malaysia The Ministry of Education (MOE) has announced additional school holidays for Diwali 2026. Students in most states will have a longer break around the Festival of Lights, though the number of days off varies by state.
 Diwali falls on Sunday, 8 November 2026 and since the festival coincides with a weekend, Monday, 9 November, has been designated a replacement public holiday. Schools in states under Group B of the 2026 academic calendar will receive an additional day off on Tuesday, 10 November. The longer break allows families to plan celebrations and travel in advance.
 Holiday arrangements by state 
 Under the 2026 Academic Calendar published by the ministry, the arrangements are divided into three categories.
 Group A includes Schools in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu will observe the replacement public holiday on Monday, 9 November.
 Group B, excluding Sarawak, includesschools in Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang, Perak, Perlis, Penang, Sabah, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya will be closed on both Monday, 9 November, and Tuesday, 10 November.
 As for Sarawak, although it falls under Group B, Sarawak will observe only the replacement public holiday on 9 November.
 These dates are provided under the festive holiday provisions of the ministry's official academic calendar.
 For families in Group B states outside Sarawak, the additional holiday creates an opportunity for a longer getaway. The break begins with the weekend on Saturday, 7 November, followed by Deepavali on Sunday, the replacement holiday on Monday and the additional school holiday on Tuesday.
 Parents on a regular Monday-to-Friday work schedule may extend their time off to four consecutive days by applying for annual leave on Tuesday, 10 November. 
 This allows more time with children, whether for returning to hometowns or taking a short holiday.
 The ministry's decision gives students in most states a longer festive break, while Sarawak and the Group A states retain a single replacement holiday. Families are encouraged to confirm their school's schedule and, where necessary, arrange leave early to make the most of the four-day period.
